detail.readme: # Buzz Your people, your agents, your projects — all in one place. Buzz is a desktop app for team chat and AI agents: join a community, talk in channels and direct messages, and run agents such as Claude, Codex, Goose or Pi on your own computer that answer you right in the conversation. [![A 38-second demo of Buzz: an agent answers a question in a team channel, then a chat with two agents is shared with that channel](docs/assets/readme/demo.webp)](https://buzz.xyz/#demo) ## Get started ### 1. Download Download the latest release from [buzz.xyz](https://buzz.xyz) or view [all releases](https://github.com/block/buzz-app/releases). Available for macOS, Windows and Linux. ### 2. Set up your identity Your identity is a private key that Buzz keeps in your system's secure storage, such as the macOS Keychain. On first launch, pick one: - **Create account** signs you up with your email. Buzz makes your key and backs it up to the account. - **Sign in** opens the key your account holds. On a new computer that works only if the key was backed up. - **Other options** starts with a community's address or invite link. A community Buzz hosts takes you to sign-in. Any other community also lets you skip the account with **Use an existing key**: paste a private key (`nsec1…`), for example from **Identity details** in Buzz 0.X. Coming from Buzz 0.X on this computer? **Other options** offers to bring its identity over in one click. **Create account** and **Sign in** bring it over only when the account has no key yet; an account that already has one keeps its own. macOS may ask you to allow Keychain access. **Check that your key is backed up.** Setup can finish without a backup, even with an account. Open **Settings → Buzz → Identity**: if it doesn't say "A backup is saved with" your account, click your private key, choose **Copy**, and keep it somewhere safe, such as a password manager. Without a backup or a copy you can't get your identity back on another computer. ### 3. Join a community After setup, Buzz asks you to **Connect to a community**: paste an invite link or a community's address. Later, use **Join a community** in the community picker, or open an invite link and choose **Accept invite in Buzz**. Coming from Buzz 0.X, Buzz also offers to import the communities you were in. **No invite?** Join the [Buzz community](https://buzz.communities.buzz.xyz/invite/v2.EeLHaUAe23P7qK0NuWnsdfnH-6L0wJLDnnzpFzrG7rQ), start your own with **Or create a community** (needs an account) or at [buzz.xyz](https://buzz.xyz), or [run your own relay](https://github.com/block/buzz#i-want-my-own-hosted-relay). ### 4. Add your first agent Open **Agents** in the app dock and choose **Create your first agent** (or **New agent → Create a new agent**). Agents belong to a community, so add yours first. Give the agent a name, pick a **Harness**, and optionally choose a model and write instructions. Then click **Create agent**. | Harness | Platforms | What you need | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude | macOS, Linux | An Anthropic API key, unless Claude already works on this computer. Click **Install integration** to download Buzz's own copy (about 250 MB), then **Add Claude API key**. It shares settings with the `claude` in your terminal but doesn't change it. | | Codex | macOS, Linux | A ChatGPT or OpenAI account. Click **Install integration** (about 130 MB), then **Sign in** in your browser. | | Goose | macOS, Linux, Windows | Included with Buzz. Choose a model provider and enter its key in **Settings → Agent setup → Harness defaults → Goose**. Providers that sign in through goose instead need `goose configure` from the separate goose CLI. | | Pi | macOS, Linux, Windows | Node.js 22.19 or later. Turn on **Pi** in **Settings → Plugins** first. Click the model, choose a provider, paste its **API key**, and click **Save to Pi**. Providers that sign in another way need `pi`, then `/login`, in your terminal. | The install and sign-in buttons appear in the create dialog, beside **Harness** or in the **Model** row, and in **Settings → Agent setup → Harness defaults**. Agents run on your computer while Buzz is open. They work in `~/.buzz` by default and can run commands and edit files there. ### 5. Talk to it - **New chat:** click **+** at the bottom of the Messages sidebar and choose **New chat**. Your default agent is tagged for you; type a message and send. - **Direct message:** open the agent's profile and click **Message**. - **In a channel:** @mention the agent. If it isn't in the channel yet, Buzz asks whether to **Invite** it. ### 6. Use the command line (optional) Buzz includes the `buzz` command line client, so scripts and agents need no separate install. On macOS and Linux (except the AppImage), Buzz links it to `~/.local/bin/buzz` each time it starts. If your shell doesn't find `buzz`, add that folder to your `PATH` in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`: ```sh export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ``` On Windows, the installer adds it to your `PATH`; open a new terminal after installing. ## Preview limitations - Releases ship every few days, and Buzz changes fast. Daily previews of `main` are on the [releases page](https://github.com/block/buzz-app/releases) for anyone who wants them earlier. - Updates can break plugins (see [Plugins](#plugins)). - The Windows installer is unsigned, and Intel macOS, Windows and Linux get less testing than Apple Silicon macOS. - Claude and Codex agents need macOS or Linux. Goose and Pi work everywhere. - Unless **Settings → Buzz → Identity** says your key is backed up, keep your own copy (step 2). - Bringing your identity over from Buzz 0.X doesn't bring your agents. On the Agents page, bring them with **Import them now** or **New agent → Import an agent**, and teams with **New team → Import a team**. ## Plugins Much of Buzz is built from plugins, and you can add your own in **Settings → Plugins**. The plugin API is a preview: Buzz changes fast, and an update can break a plugin. Some parts change less than others: - **Steady:** the manifest, commands, network requests and file reads, agent tools, shortcuts, notifications, settings cards, and plugin pages and panels (though where they appear may move). - **Likely to break:** reading relay data, anything added to conversations or the sidebar, agent hooks, and UI added to pages Buzz owns. See [plugins](docs/plugins.md) to build one. ## Build from source ```sh git clone https://github.com/block/buzz-app.git cd buzz-app bin/just desktop ``` Hermit in `bin/` pins every tool. Desktop builds also need the [Tauri prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/). See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup, live relay development, testing and hooks, and [plugins](docs/plugins.md) to build plugins. ## Project resources - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Plugins](docs/plugins.md) - [Contextual identity names: cross-client spec and fixtures](src/bundled/identity-naming/README.md) - [Mention rules: cross-client spec and fixtures](src/bundled/mentions/README.md) - [@buzzdotxyz on X](https://x.com/buzzdotxyz) - [Project leads](CODEOWNERS) - [Governance](GOVERNANCE.md) - [Apache-2.0 license](LICENSE) - [Source attribution](NOTICE.md)
